teams.heading: Fiji scoring average drops following three consecutive Nations Championship defeats
teams.body: Fiji have averaged 28.5 points scored and 31.9 points conceded per game across their last 11 senior men’s internationals. This scoring rate has declined during the current campaign; the side has averaged just over 16 points per match across their three recent losses. In the broader 11-game window, the team’s most significant result remains the 63-10 win against Canada recorded in September 2025. Fiji currently sit bottom of the table following their 17-33 defeat to Scotland.

teams.heading: Premiership clubs agree law interpretation overhaul to aid Steve Borthwick's England
teams.body: Premiership directors of rugby have agreed to align domestic refereeing with the international game to support Steve Borthwick’s World Cup preparations. Following a meeting with Borthwick, officials will now prioritise stricter policing of the offside line, the breakdown, and the scrum’s brake-foot law. The revamp aims to address inconsistencies that hindered England during the Six Nations and better prepare the squad for the ferocity of Test rugby ahead of next year’s tournament in Australia.

teams.heading: Sean Jansen commits to Connacht as Ireland back-rower signs extension
teams.body: Ireland number eight Sean Jansen has signed a two-year contract extension, keeping him with Connacht until at least 2029. The 27-year-old, who made his international debut against Japan this summer, enjoyed a standout campaign last season, scoring 12 tries in 20 appearances. Connacht head coach Stuart Lancaster described the deal as a “massive boost” for the province, citing Jansen’s recent form and commitment as a major statement of intent ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season.

teams.heading: Italy Men Face World Champion South Africa At Allianz Stadium Venue
teams.body: Top-level international rugby is set to return to the Allianz Stadium this November. Following the official presentation held on Sunday, 20 September, it was confirmed that Italy will host reigning world champions South Africa at the home of Juventus. This fixture marks the Azzurri’s first home match of the 2026 Nations Championship. Gonzalo Quesada’s side will utilise the Turin venue to kick off a demanding autumn series before continuing their campaign with further tests in Genoa and Udine.

teams.heading: Professional players express ongoing frustration regarding smaller ball trial adoption plans
teams.body: The trial of the smaller ball in the WXV Global Series continues to draw scrutiny from international players. While World Rugby has moved to expand the testing period, concerns regarding the performance impact persist. Players have been vocal about the transition, with England fly-half Zoe Harrison describing the change as the worst decision ever. With the trial period set to conclude in October, stakeholders remain divided on whether this adjustment is a viable long-term solution for the women’s game.

teams.heading: Wales women lose scrum-half Seren Lockwood for upcoming USA Test match
teams.body: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has confirmed that scrum-half Seren Lockwood will miss Saturday's WXV Global Series fixture against the USA at Cardiff Arms Park. Lockwood, named Wales women's young player of the year, is currently progressing through World Rugby's return to play protocols following a head injury assessment. Her absence sees Lleucu George return to the starting lineup at 10, with Keira Bevan shifting to her familiar role at nine for the encounter against the visitors.

teams.heading: Japan Men Claim Pacific Nations Cup Title After Defeating Fiji
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 with a 20-15 victory over holders Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. Captain Naoto Saito hailed the milestone as a breakthrough moment for the squad. "All I was thinking about was winning this game. I'm glad we won today, and it's a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. It gives this young team great confidence," Saito said. The win also lifts Japan into the World Rugby top ten rankings.

teams.heading: Scott Barrett set to make long-awaited return for Taranaki this weekend
teams.body: Former All Blacks skipper Scott Barrett is back to full fitness and will return to action in a National Provincial Championship game for Taranaki. Barrett has been sidelined for the entire season with a back injury and will start at lock in Taranaki's clash against Hawke's Bay at McLean Park in Napier on Sunday. The 32-year-old was last in action for the men in black against Wales at the end of 2025 and subsequently underwent surgery for a bulging disc that had left his left side depowered.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen captains heavily changed Springboks side to face Wallabies
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to his starting XV for Sunday's Test against the Wallabies in Perth, naming Andre Esterhuizen as captain in the absence of Siya Kolisi. The 32-year-old midfielder leads an overhauled lineup featuring only two survivors from the win over the All Blacks in Baltimore, with Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker retaining their starting spots. Erasmus has packed his replacements bench with frontline experience, including Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche, and Jasper Wiese, who is set to earn his 50th Test cap.
